title: Treasure Chest
story: You're building a dungeon crawler. Every treasure chest contains loot: gold coins, gems (with names like "Ruby"), potions (with effects like "Healing"), or just junk. Each loot type has a different gold value. You need to open random chests and tally your riches.
why: An enum with both simple variants and data-carrying variants models randomized loot systems perfectly.
analogy: Loot is like your trick-or-treat bag after Halloween. Gold is actual coins. Gems are the full-size chocolate bars (valuable!). Potions are the gummy candies (decent). Junk is the toothbrush some neighbor always hands out (worthless). The value method is you sorting the bag on the living room floor.
try_it: Add a `Weapon(name: Str, damage: Int)` variant. Add a `Loot.is_valuable(self) -> Bool` method (value > 100). Simulate opening 5 chests: Gold(25), Gem("Ruby"), Potion("Strength"), Weapon("Sword", 25), Junk. Tally everything.
tips: Use `if/if/else` chains for gem/potion subcategories � match inside match is valid but nested
Junk carries no data and has no value � the simplest possible variant
The value method returns different amounts for different gem names � this shows multi-level matching
common_mistakes: Returning 200 for all gems � the value should depend on the gem name (Ruby=200, Diamond=500)
Forgetting to check all potion types � unknown potions should still return a reasonable default (20)
